step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified user actors and entry points: User icon at top mapped to UserConsumerWeb, accessing AWS ALB.
2. Analyzed traffic split at ALB: User traffic splits into two pathways: internal end-user traffic routed to Zscaler (EC2) for identity and access control, and partner/B2B traffic routed to Firewall (EC2) and then to WAF.
3. Identified target application workloads: Both paths lead down to Enterprise Applications (EC2 instances running SAP and other core applications).
4. Mapped hybrid connectivity: On-premise data center (OnPremDC) connects via AWS Direct Connect (DX) into the AWS cloud environment towards Zscaler and enterprise apps.
5. Mapped security and alerting flow: GuardDuty monitors VPC infrastructure events, triggering a Lambda function that filters critical alerts and sends notifications to a third-party Mobile Alert App.
6. Formulated nodes and logical flow-segmented edges with strict vocabulary compliance.

graph.name: Tata Global Beverages AWS Enterprise Application Migration & Security Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture showing Tata Global Beverages' migration of enterprise workloads to AWS, featuring dual ingress paths (Zscaler for internal users, Firewall+WAF for B2B/partners), Direct Connect hybrid link, and automated security alerting via GuardDuty, Lambda, and mobile chat app.

nodes.name: ALB

nodes.name: ZSCALER
nodes.notes: Zscaler cloud security broker running on EC2, enforcing user-to-application granular access control integrated with Azure AD MFA

nodes.name: FIREWALL
nodes.notes: Firewall EC2 instance processing B2B traffic from modern trade partners and customers

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: AWS WAF inspecting web application traffic routed from the firewall

nodes.name: DX
nodes.notes: AWS Direct Connect providing dedicated connection between on-premises and AWS cloud workloads

nodes.name: GUARDDUTY
nodes.notes: AWS GuardDuty continuously monitoring VPC infrastructure and transaction logs

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: AWS Lambda function filtering critical GuardDuty security alerts

nodes.name: Mobile Alert App
nodes.notes: Third-party mobile chat application receiving real-time group security alerts

nodes.name: ENT. APPS SAP
nodes.notes: Enterprise application workloads, including SAP, running on standardized EC2 instances

edges.notes: End users send application requests to ALB
ALB routes internal user requests to Zscaler
ALB routes B2B partner and customer requests to Firewall
Zscaler forwards authenticated and authorized user traffic directly to enterprise applications
Firewall passes incoming B2B web traffic to AWS WAF for inspection
Inspected B2B traffic is delivered to Enterprise Applications
On-premises data center sends network traffic over AWS Direct Connect
Direct Connect routes traffic securely to cloud applications via Zscaler layer
GuardDuty triggers Lambda upon detecting security threats
Lambda filters critical alerts and sends instant notifications to mobile chat app
